subject: Residency annex & transient backup egress clarifications
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
To: Maria Lopez <maria.lopez@healthsys.com>, Legal Team <legal@healthsys.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 15 Jun 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Residency annex & transient backup egress clarifications

Hi Maria / HealthSys legal team,

Thanks again for the productive call earlier. A couple of follow-ups from our side to make sure the DPA annex lines up with your residency requirements for the EU environment:

1) Production pinning: HealthSys requested EU-only placement for production workloads. Can you confirm that the annex should include an explicit "region-pin: EU" commitment for all production model inference and associated analytics telemetry?

2) Transient backups / DR windows: We typically replicate encrypted backups to a cross-region DR location for durability. For EU customers we can limit transient replication to non-EU regions only under a short, defined window. We need to align on an acceptable window (we default to 72 hours for automated snapshots during a failover test). Would HealthSys accept up to 72h for automated snapshot replication for DR, provided the data is encrypted in transit and at rest and key material remains under your KMS scope?

3) Subprocessors: Attached is our current subprocessor roster and a draft DPA annex (Redwood_DPA_Annex_v0.3.pdf and subprocessor_roster_20280615.csv). Please let us know if you need additional detail (SOC2 reports, location of hosting for each subprocessor).

4) Escrow / temporary exception flow: If there are narrow situations where a longer retention is required (e.g., declared incident or legal hold) we'll follow an exception workflow and seek written approval + logging evidence. We can include the exception flow as an exhibit to the annex.

Action requested: can Legal confirm the max transient egress window you would accept and whether HealthSys requires split-key custody for backups (customer-held KMS) or is okay with Redwood-managed KMS keys with CMKs provided?

I can set up a 30m follow-up with our legal/ops folks if helpful.

Thanks,
Jordan Blake
Senior Sales Engineer
Redwood Inference

Attachments: Redwood_DPA_Annex_v0.3.pdf; subprocessor_roster_20280615.csv; runbook-dr-backup-overview.pdf
From: Maria Lopez <maria.lopez@healthsys.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
Cc: Legal Team <legal@healthsys.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 16 Jun 2028 08:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Residency annex & transient backup egress clarifications

Hi Jordan —

Appreciate the attachments and the clear summary. Quick responses from Legal/Privacy after a first pass:

- Production pinning: yes, HealthSys requires a binding clause that production inference and related telemetry for HealthSys accounts are anchored to EU data centers (subject to outage failover constraints). We expect the annex to state the scope (models, embeddings, telemetry).

- Transient backups / DR: Legal is cautious about the 72h default. Their current ask is a maximum of 48 hours for automated replication to non-EU regions, unless a declared incident/approved exception is invoked. They also request audit evidence (timestamped transfer logs) for every transient transfer.

- Subprocessors: please provide the granular roster with hosting countries and certs (SOC2/ISO). If any subprocessor would process EU-origin data in the US, Legal wants that explicitly flagged.

Attached is a short questionnaire our legal team completed as initial questions (HealthSys-DPA-questions.pdf). We will need a redline of the annex; could you produce a version with the 48h window and the logging commitments so our counsel can review?

Thanks — looping in our Legal team.

Best,
Maria Lopez
Sr. Privacy Program Manager
HealthSys

Attachments: HealthSys-DPA-questions.pdf
From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
To: Maria Lopez <maria.lopez@healthsys.com>, Legal Team <legal@healthsys.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 16 Jun 2028 09:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Residency annex & transient backup egress clarifications

Thanks Maria — and thanks for the quick read from Legal.

On the 48h ask: we can accept 48 hours as the standard upper bound for automated transient replication for EU accounts, with the following proposals to cover operational reality:

- Standard window = 48h for automated snapshot replication.
- Incident exception = up to 120h for declared incidents that require forensic analysis or cross-region recovery, but only with documented approval from HealthSys Security + an automated expiring authorization token (we'll include the exception process in the annex exhibit).
- Logging / evidence = Redwood will provide per-transfer logs (timestamp, source region, destination region, object id, transfer size) and retain those audit logs for 12 months unless HealthSys requests a different retention. Logs will be surfaced via a secure link (we can add a Drive snapshot URL and a signed hash manifest for transfer batches).
- Key custody = for EU accounts we recommend customer-managed keys (bring-your-own CMK) in your KMS; if you prefer Redwood-managed keys we can provide split-key escrow or a written attestation of access controls.

Next steps I propose (mutual action plan):
- Redwood: produce redline of annex with 48h window + exception exhibit + logging clause (I'll own the redline).
- HealthSys: indicate whether you require customer KMS CMK or accept Redwood-managed keys with split-key escrow.
- Legal review: exchange final redline via DocuSign for the annex signature.

I've attached an updated annex draft (Redwood_DPA_Annex_v0.3.pdf) with inline comments and the subprocessor CSV. I'll prepare a redline with the 48h language and send by EOD your time. Would you be available for a 30m call Monday to finalize?

Jordan Blake
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
T: (415) 555-0119

Attachments: Redwood_DPA_Annex_v0.3.pdf; subprocessor_roster_20280615.csv; runbook-dr-backup-overview.pdf

Date: Sat, 16 Jun 2028 10:25:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Residency annex & transient backup egress clarifications

Thanks Jordan / Maria —

I'll take point on the redline. Jordan: I'll prepare a clean redline that implements the 48h standard window, adds the incident exception exhibit language (120h with approvals), and inserts the logging clause. I will also include a short checklist of required subprocessors evidence (hosting country + SOC2 link) so HealthSys Legal can tick boxes.

Maria: would you prefer a shared DocuSign link or a tracked Google doc for initial review? I can spin up the doc and invite your counsel.

Will follow up with the draft redline by end of day Monday.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Head of Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference
